items.hook: Polymeric N3H2, a single-bonded nitrogen solid, was synthesized at about 139 GPa.
items.summary: Squeezing nitrogen and hydrogen mixtures to 134 to 139 GPa produced a solid made of chains of N6 rings, each carrying four hydrogen atoms and linked by hydrogen bonds. Synchrotron single-crystal diffraction located the hydrogen atoms directly, and Raman spectroscopy and calculations support the structure. The 7.98 kJ/g decomposition energy is an estimate, and the material was made only under extreme pressure, not recovered to ambient conditions.
items.title: High-pressure synthesis of a polymeric N3H2 solid stabilized by hydrogen bonds

items.hook: A polarity-switching phthalimide lets four-electron Li-I2 pouch cells run past 1000 cycles.
items.summary: A phthalimide molecule changes from electron-poor to electron-rich as the battery charges, first trapping iodine species to stop them shuttling, then stabilizing the reactive I+ state. Flexible Li-I2 pouch cells reached about 400 mAh per gram of iodine and over 1200 Wh per kg of iodine. Cathode-level energy is lower, at about 883 Wh per kg, and results are for lab-scale cells.
items.title: Switchable nucleophile-electrophile chemistry enables functional four-electron Li-I2 batteries

items.hook: Phosphorus-doped silicon nanoantennas detect 1.55 micrometer light, all in silicon at room temperature.
items.summary: Patterning heavily phosphorus-doped silicon into nanoantenna arrays shifts its plasmonic resonances into the 1 to 2 micrometer range. Detectors built from them respond at 1.55 micrometers. The responsivity comes from plasmon-enhanced absorption plus trap-assisted gain under bias, so it does not reflect the intrinsic quantum efficiency.
items.title: Near-infrared plasmonic response in hyperdoped silicon nanoantennas for all-silicon photodetection

items.hook: Synthetic vesicles swim away from a chemical signal with no catalyst or outside energy.
items.summary: A minimal polymer vesicle shows negative chemotaxis, moving away from a chemical cue because its hydrophobic membrane domains rearrange and shift interfacial tension. This offers a molecular mechanism for artificial motility that mimics cytoskeletal remodeling. The abstract gives no quantitative performance, and the system is a simplified lab model, far from a living protocell.
items.title: Conformationally driven negative chemotaxis in synthetic vesicles.

items.hook: An organic semiconductor sheet split water under simulated sunlight for over 2 hours, at 0.1% efficiency.
items.summary: One solution-processed organic blend drives either hydrogen or oxygen evolution depending on the molecular contact layer beneath it. A patterned underlayer combining both reactions gave unassisted water splitting at 1.3 micromoles per hour per square centimeter. The 0.1% solar-to-hydrogen efficiency is low and was shown for only a couple of hours under simulated light.
items.title: An organic semiconductor-based photocatalyst sheet for overall solar-driven water splitting

items.hook: Metamaterials with wildly varied strut lengths and thicknesses absorb more energy and steer waves.
items.summary: Borrowing ideas from network science, the authors design mechanical metamaterials whose ligament lengths, thicknesses and connectivity vary over orders of magnitude, controlled by just two parameters. Simulations and experiments show tunable stiffness direction, spread-out deformation with high energy absorption, and programmable elastic-wave control. Tests were on lab-made samples, so large-scale manufacturing is untested.
items.title: Scale-rich network-based metamaterials.

items.hook: The CMG helicase hands human PRIMPOL to the leading strand to restart stalled DNA replication.
items.summary: Using purified human proteins to rebuild a stalled replication fork, the authors show that PRIMPOL binds directly to the CMG helicase, which aims it at leading-strand priming and keeps the leftover DNA gaps small. A cryo-electron microscopy structure shows the contact, and breaking it abolishes restart in vitro and PRIMPOL-dependent damage tolerance in human cells. The reconstitution is simplified compared with a living cell.
items.title: Human replisomes direct a dedicated leading-strand primase for fork restart.

items.hook: Luminal breast tumors hide a basal-like cell subpopulation, and blood nucleosome marks may flag it.
items.summary: Single-cell epigenetic profiling of untreated luminal tumors found a recurring subpopulation of basal-like cells with aggressive traits and lower hormone receptor signaling. Histone H3K4 methylation marks tracked the loss of luminal identity, and the same signature measured in cell-free nucleosomes in blood was linked to relapse risk. The cohort is limited to surgical patients, and the blood test is a proof of concept.
items.title: Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis.

items.hook: China's one vote veto policy explains nearly half of the 1990s fertility decline.
items.summary: The one-child policy had little early effect on fertility, but the authors find it bit once officials faced career penalties for failing to comply. Using differences in when provinces adopted the veto, they attribute nearly half of the 1990s drop to it, mostly through official-recommended IUD use. This is a statistical inference from policy timing, so other regional changes could still contribute.
items.title: Bureaucratic incentives shaped effectiveness of the one-child policy in China.

items.hook: Clinical obesity carried 1.69 times the death risk, preclinical only 1.19, across 844,108 adults.
items.summary: Applying the 2025 Lancet Commission definitions to four cohorts in China, the UK, the USA and Spain, the authors found that adding waist measures to BMI changes who counts as obese. Clinical obesity, with organ dysfunction, was tied to much higher all-cause mortality than preclinical obesity, and most preclinical cases did not progress over 10 years. These are observational associations, not proof of cause.
items.title: Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts.

items.hook: Mouse two-cell embryo nuclei turn soft as LC3 clears lamin B1, helping switch on zygotic genes.
items.summary: Direct nuclear capture and biophysical tests show that nuclei in two-cell mouse embryos become very soft because the autophagy factor LC3 removes lamin B1 from the nuclear envelope. Stiffening the nucleus, by keeping lamin B1 or adding an engineered tether, leaves zygotic genes incompletely activated and impairs development. The work is in mouse embryos, and human relevance is untested.
items.title: Transient nuclear softening for zygotic gene activation in mice.

items.hook: A calibration-free imaging method recovers the M87* black hole ring, 42.2 microarcseconds wide.

readout.label: Angular diameter of the M87* ring

items.summary: An independent algorithm uses observables immune to instrument calibration errors and avoids built-in assumptions about shape. Applied to the Event Horizon Telescope M87* data, it reproduces a ring, implying a black hole mass of 6.5 billion suns. The mass depends on nominal scaling parameters, and the sparse interferometric data limit how fine the details can be.
items.title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87.

items.hook: Blocking mitochondrial protein import makes melanoma cells easier for T cells to spot, in models.
items.summary: Depleting the import subunit TIMM50 lets mitochondrial DNA escape, which activates cGAS-STING, interferon-beta release and more MHC class I antigen display. This synergized with checkpoint blockade in melanoma models. The evidence is from cell and mouse models, and a safe way to inhibit import in patients is not shown.
items.title: Mitochondrial protein import defects enhance tumour immunogenicity.

items.hook: Antisense drugs fixing one UNC13A splicing error restore synapse function in TDP-43-depleted neurons.
items.summary: Losing TDP-43 leaves neurons intact but with failing synaptic communication, and correcting a single cryptic splicing event in UNC13A rescued this. Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides restored vesicle release and network synchrony in human cortical and motor neurons, and worked in a humanized mouse model. Benefit in patients is untested, and the work covers cultured neurons and mice.
items.title: UNC13A splice correction rescues synaptic dysfunction induced by TDP-43 loss.

items.hook: Rice detects RNA fragments from stink bug saliva with a protein that forms condensates and triggers defense
items.hook_turn: forms condensates and triggers defense
items.summary: Sucking insects inject RNases that cut RNA into cyclic nucleotide fragments. The rice protein NIB1 binds these fragments, forms nuclear condensates, and recruits the immune regulator EDS1. Shown with genetics and biochemistry in rice and one insect species. The link to TIR protein signaling is only suggested.
items.title: A plant RNA-binding protein senses 2',3'-cNMP produced by insect effectors.

items.hook: A drug that forces androgen receptor and p300/CBP together shrinks prostate tumors in mice
items.hook_turn: shrinks prostate tumors in mice
items.summary: DALTAC-1 joins two proteins that normally cooperate at the wrong interface, locking them in an inactive state. It blocked androgen-driven gene activity and growth more strongly than inhibiting each protein separately, and spared cells lacking the receptor. Tumor regressions were seen in mouse models only, so human safety and benefit are unknown.
items.title: Domain-alteration chimeras rewire oncogenic complexes in prostate cancer.

items.hook: Mice lacking IgA get more colon tumors, and IgA works by tempering gut cell growth through DMBT1
items.hook_turn: IgA works by tempering gut cell growth through DMBT1
items.summary: IgA-deficient mice were more prone to several colorectal cancer models. Oral IgA restored normal gut cell proliferation by acting on the epithelial protein DMBT1, found through a CRISPR screen, regardless of what the antibody binds. All results are in mice and cultured cells, so the role in human IgA deficiency is untested.
items.title: Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA.

items.hook: Counting severe drought raises the share of cactus species losing habitat from about 60% to about 70%
items.hook_turn: raises the share of cactus species losing habitat from about 60% to about 70%

readout.label: Cases where drought models fit better

items.summary: Researchers added severe-drought data to distribution models for 993 cactus species using 648,316 occurrence records. Models with drought fit better in 91% of cases and projected more species losing suitable climate, especially with no dispersal. These are model projections of climate suitability, not observed extinctions.
items.title: Severe drought and warming increase the extinction risk of cacti.

items.hook: Blood clones with several cancer driver mutations can sweep the blood decades before leukemia is diagnosed
items.hook_turn: can sweep the blood decades before leukemia is diagnosed
items.summary: Yearly blood samples taken up to 15 years before acute myeloid leukemia diagnosis were deep-sequenced and fitted with evolutionary theory. First drivers arise early in life and grow slowly, while later drivers give up to 100-fold larger growth advantages. The cohort is limited to people who went on to develop leukemia, so predictive power in the general population is not established.
items.title: Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia.

items.hook: A single-crystal TiO2 gate insulator lets 2D transistors switch near the thermal limit with tiny standby power
items.hook_turn: lets 2D transistors switch near the thermal limit with tiny standby power
items.summary: A wafer-scale anatase titanium dioxide dielectric was transferred onto 2D semiconductors with a clean interface. Both n- and p-type transistors showed near-ideal subthreshold swing and very low hysteresis, and inverters drew subpicowatt static power. Demonstrated on individual devices and simple inverters, not large circuits.
items.title: Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics.

items.hook: Single-molecule movies show PRIMPOL restarts stalled DNA copying by hitching onto the replicative helicase
items.hook_turn: restarts stalled DNA copying by hitching onto the replicative helicase
items.summary: PRIMPOL lets cells skip DNA damage by starting a new primer ahead of the lesion. Imaging in nuclear extracts showed it is recruited by the CMG helicase, then hands the primer to the accurate polymerase ε. This was observed in cell extracts rather than intact cells.
items.title: The molecular basis of replication fork restart via repriming by PRIMPOL.

items.hook: A 1.5-mm metasurface waveguide gives AR glasses a 30° field of view and a bright image outdoors
items.hook_turn: gives AR glasses a 30° field of view and a bright image outdoors
items.summary: Interwoven metasurfaces in two layers steer light in several directions, easing the usual trade-off among field of view, brightness, and eyebox. The prototype reaches a 30° field of view and an 8 by 8 mm eyebox. It is a single prototype, and the field of view is still modest.
items.title: Metasurface waveguides for all-day augmented reality glasses.

items.hook: Flexible rubber turbine blades match pitch-controlled rigid ones in yield with a third less load jitter
items.hook_turn: with a third less load jitter
items.summary: Blades that bend at the trailing edge flatten under load, passively easing fatigue-causing fluctuations by up to one-third. In experiments over simulated tidal cycles, energy yield matched rigid blades with active pitch control. Tests were lab-scale with simulated tides, not a turbine at sea.
items.title: Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines.

items.hook: North China gneiss dated to 3.95 billion years hints at a brief subduction event in the Hadean
items.hook_turn: hints at a brief subduction event in the Hadean
items.summary: Zircon in a gneiss from Hebei records oxygen and hafnium signatures of altered crust that was buried deep (above 1.6 GPa) along a cool path. That points to a transient subduction event, only the second known rock above 3.9 billion years. The subduction reading comes from modeling and one rock unit.
items.title: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks.

items.hook: Water-based zinc and aluminum iodine batteries run four-electron iodine chemistry without halogen salts
items.hook_turn: run four-electron iodine chemistry without halogen salts
items.summary: Four-electron iodine conversion stores more energy but usually needs corrosive halogen-rich electrolytes. A designed mix of polar, kosmotropic, and nucleophilic species stabilizes the reactive iodine cations through halogen bonds. Shown in lab cells, so cycle life and scale-up are open.
items.title: Non-halogen aqueous electrolytes for four-electron iodine conversion.

items.hook: Tapirs and anteaters living near development carry more microplastics in blood, and remote ones have some
items.hook_turn: carry more microplastics in blood, and remote ones have some
items.summary: Microplastic levels measured in free-ranging lowland tapirs and giant anteaters in Brazil rose with human footprint exposure and nearness to waste infrastructure, using GPS tracking. Animals in seemingly pristine areas also had microplastics. Two species and observational data, so causes are not isolated.
items.title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife.

items.hook: Cold lowers IL-1β and flips brown fat cells to a high-heat state, and aged fat stays stuck in the low state
items.hook_turn: aged fat stays stuck in the low state
items.summary: IL-1β from immune cells keeps some brown fat cells at low UCP1 through a glucocorticoid pathway. Cold reduces IL-1β, switching these cells to high heat output, but old mice have too much IL-1β. Blocking the glucocorticoid receptor restored heat production in aged mice. Mouse work only.
items.title: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis.

items.hook: Stiff-matrix culture reveals NRF2 as a switch that lets one signal turn on the NLRP3 inflammasome
items.hook_turn: NRF2 as a switch that lets one signal turn on the NLRP3 inflammasome
items.summary: Lab cultures need two signals to activate NLRP3, but animals need only one. Growing macrophages on tissue-like stiffness induced NRF2, which acts via Panx1 to enable one-signal activation. Supporting data came from human lung samples and mouse cancer vaccines, but mostly from cells and mice.
items.title: NRF2 is a mechanosensitive checkpoint for NLRP3 inflammasome activation.

items.hook: A palladium catalyst attaches aryl groups to plain arenes at the most open C-H site.
items.hook_turn: at the most open C-H site.
items.summary: A palladium catalyst system joins aryl groups directly to C-H bonds in simple arenes, favoring the sterically most exposed site. It pairs a tailored catalyst environment with an advanced precatalyst and diaryliodonium reagents. Even benzene can be arylated repeatedly, and mild conditions allow late-stage use and groups that normal cross-coupling would destroy. Scope is shown on selected substrates, so performance on other molecules is untested.
items.title: Efficient catalyst-controlled C-H arylation of arenes.

items.hook: Nearly half of BRCA1 variants that look broken in one cell line score neutral in breast cells.
items.hook_turn: score neutral in breast cells.
items.summary: The team edited BRCA1 across the gene in HAP1 cells, scoring 4,113 previously unassayed variants, and built a matching assay in mammary epithelial cells. Variants that disagreed between the two cell types behaved as hypomorphs, partly reduced in function, and tracked with intermediate cancer risk. The scores are lab measurements in cultured cells, not outcomes in patients.
items.title: Saturation genome editing of BRCA1 across cell types improves interpretation of variant pathogenicity.

items.hook: A digital pathology score of TROP2 location in tumor cells predicts who benefits from datopotamab deruxtecan.
items.hook_turn: predicts who benefits from datopotamab deruxtecan.
items.summary: A computer-vision method measures how much TROP2 sits on the cell membrane versus the cytoplasm in lung tumor slides. Patients scoring positive had longer progression-free survival on the antibody-drug conjugate (median 7.2 vs 4.0 months) but not on docetaxel. The cut-point was tuned and tested within retrospective analyses of trial samples, so it needs prospective confirmation.
items.title: Normalized membrane ratio of TROP2 as a predictor of clinical outcomes with datopotamab deruxtecan in non-small-cell lung cancer.

items.hook: A personalized neoantigen vaccine plus pembrolizumab cut melanoma recurrence in a phase 3 trial.
items.hook_turn: cut melanoma recurrence in a phase 3 trial.
items.summary: In 1137 patients with resected stage IIB to IV melanoma, adding the individualized therapy intismeran to pembrolizumab raised 24-month recurrence-free survival from 70.0% to 82.2% versus placebo. The benefit appeared only after about 6 months, and serious adverse events were slightly more common (23.6% vs 20.3%). Follow-up is a median of 24.6 months, so overall survival is not yet known.
items.title: Intismeran Autogene plus Pembrolizumab for Resected Stage IIB to IV Melanoma.

items.hook: Microbial community dynamics seen through a few observables compress into surprisingly few latent dimensions.
items.hook_turn: into surprisingly few latent dimensions.
items.summary: Variational autoencoders were used to find the smallest latent dimension that reconstructs observed microbial population dynamics. That dimension was far below the community's apparent complexity and grew linearly with the number of observables. The pattern held across simulations, engineered and environmental communities, and human microbiomes, but it supports only selected prediction tasks.
items.title: Linear scaling reveals low-dimensional structure in observable microbial dynamics.
items.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.hook: Easing DNA supercoiling strain by lowering TOP1 activity boosts how much MYC amplifies transcription.
items.hook_turn: boosts how much MYC amplifies transcription.
items.summary: The authors built a system that separates MYC's activation of specific genes from its general amplification of transcription. Cutting TOP1 activity by knockdown or low-dose inhibitor strengthened amplification, apparently because negative supercoiling aids promoter melting and polymerase loading. The evidence comes from cell and biochemical assays, not whole organisms.
items.title: Dynamic supercoiling sponsors transcription amplification by MYC.
items.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.hook: Two prefrontal circuits in mice separately curb drinking, anxiety and low mood, with PPP1R1B as a key switch.
items.hook_turn: with PPP1R1B as a key switch.
items.summary: In mice drinking alcohol intermittently, activating a prelimbic-to-accumbens pathway reduced drinking, anxiety and depression-like behavior, while an infralimbic-to-amygdala pathway affected drinking and anxiety only. Protein profiling pointed to PPP1R1B, and knocking it out or overexpressing it in those neurons reproduced or reversed the behaviors. Results are in mice over four weeks, so human relevance is untested.
items.title: PPP1R1B differentially modulates alcohol intake and emotional comorbidity through distinct prefrontal circuits.
items.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.hook: Paramecium sonneborni carries chromosome-sized DNA from species too distant to normally interbreed.
items.hook_turn: from species too distant to normally interbreed.
items.summary: Genome analysis of P. sonneborni found hundreds of segments, some near chromosome length, from very distant paramecium lineages, which points to repeated mating across species. The authors propose paramecia tolerate this because foreign DNA is stripped from the somatic nucleus. The mechanism is inferred from genome sequences, not tested by crossing.
items.title: Recurrent hybridization between highly divergent paramecium species.
items.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.hook: Human cells exposed to low hydrogen sulfide store carbon in lipid droplets to offset redox stress.
items.hook_turn: to offset redox stress.
items.summary: Chronic exposure to 4 to 20 micromolar H2S shifted NAD and coenzyme Q pools toward the reduced state and drove triglyceride buildup in lipid droplets across several human cell lines. Blocking fatty acid synthesis during exposure impaired recovery of respiration. This was seen in cultured cells, so the link to gut sulfide and metabolic health remains a hypothesis.
items.title: Lipid droplets buffer hydrogen sulfide-induced redox imbalance.
items.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.hook: A Cauchy walk finds 3D targets of nearly any shape close to optimally.
items.hook_turn: of nearly any shape close to optimally.
items.summary: Random searchers that mix short steps with rare long jumps (Levy walks) find 3D targets at speeds that depend on target volume, surface area, and elongation. The authors prove that the Cauchy walk, a particular Levy walk, matches the best possible detection time up to polylogarithmic factors for convex targets, while other walks fall short in some regimes. This is a mathematical result for idealized convex targets, not a test on real animals or cells.
items.title: Intermittent Cauchy walks enable optimal 3D search across target shapes and sizes.
items.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.hook: Dryland shrub and grass ecosystems behave like matter in phase transitions.
items.hook_turn: behave like matter in phase transitions.
items.summary: Deserts, shrublands, and grasslands are separated by abrupt shifts, and the latter two form Turing-like patterns, with fairy circles near the shrub-grass boundary. A cellular automaton built on a trade-off between wide and local resource foraging reproduces these features, and plant traits and patch patterns support the trade-off. The model is simplified, so the match shows consistency with the theory rather than proof of the mechanism.
items.title: Phase transition in a dryland shrub-grass ecosystem: Emergence through local trade-offs.
items.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.hook: Enzymes known for editing chromatin co-evolved with cytoskeleton proteins, and NSD3 binds tubulin.
items.hook_turn: and NSD3 binds tubulin.
items.summary: Comparing which genes are conserved together across species, the authors found that human methyltransferases track with many cytoskeletal components. This pointed to an unexpected link, and they confirmed experimentally that the methyltransferase NSD3 associates with alpha-tubulin. Only one prediction was tested in the lab, and whether the link has a functional role remains open.
items.title: Phylogenetic profiling reveals evolutionary coupling between methyltransferases and the cytoskeleton.
items.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
